data.content:
Obsidian
Obsidian is a personal knowledge management system that allows users to capture, store, and connect information in a digital vault, with features such as version control using git, AI-searchable capabilities, and synchronization through GitHub.<SEP>A personal knowledge management and note-taking app.<SEP>A note-taking and knowledge management application.

Git
Git is a version control system that allows users to track changes to their files and collaborate with others on projects.<SEP>A version control system.

GitHub
GitHub is a web-based platform for version control and collaboration on software development projects.<SEP>GitHub is also used for synchronization of the Obsidian vault.<SEP>A web-based platform for version control and collaboration.

Copilot
Copilot is an AI-powered coding assistant that can provide suggestions and complete code for users.<SEP>A plugin for Obsidian that allows for chat with the vault.

Smart Connections
Smart Connections is a feature of Obsidian that allows users to connect related notes and ideas.<SEP>A plugin for Obsidian that embeds related notes and offers semantic search.

MCP
MCP stands for "Meaningful Content Platform" and is a feature of Obsidian that allows users to create and connect concept notes.<SEP>Machine learning concept.<SEP>A network protocol used for remote access and management of devices.

SETUP.md
SETUP.md is a document that provides setup instructions for the Obsidian vault.

system.md
system.md is a document that provides information about the workflow of the Obsidian vault.

Hebrew
Hebrew is a language that is being studied in the Obsidian vault.

Russian
Russian is a language that is being studied in the Obsidian vault.

Arabic
Arabic is a language that is being studied in the Obsidian vault.

German
German is a language that is being studied in the Obsidian vault.

Ollama
A large language model.

Claude Desktop
A desktop AI assistant.

Node.js
A JavaScript runtime environment.

tarik
The user who set up the Obsidian vault.

Templater
A plugin for Obsidian that allows for templates with code.

QuickAdd
A plugin for Obsidian that allows for one hotkey to capture into a specific folder.

Dataview
A plugin for Obsidian that allows for querying notes like a database.

Spaced Repetition
A plugin for Obsidian that allows for flashcards inside notes.

Obsidian Git
A plugin for Obsidian that allows for auto-commit, push, and pull to GitHub.

Local REST API
A plugin for Obsidian that allows for the Obsidian-specific MCP server.

MCP server
A server that allows for the Obsidian-specific MCP server.

Windows
An operating system used by the user.<SEP>Windows is the operating system where the evtx-analyst tool is used to parse logs.

WSL
A Linux environment on Windows.<SEP>A Linux environment for Windows.

github.com
The website for the GitHub platform.

Obsidian Sync
A paid service for official, end-to-end encrypted syncing.

Syncthing
A free, peer-to-peer syncing service.

Claude Code
A coding assistant.

Tarik
The user, managing their Obsidian vault.

Claude
A coding assistant.

Concept
Notes on various learning concepts, including MCP and Reverse-Engineering.

Reverse-Engineering
Method of understanding how a system works by analyzing its components.<SEP>The process of analyzing and reverse-engineering software or systems to understand their internal workings.

Go
Programming concept or game.<SEP>A programming language developed by Google.

_index
Front page of learning notes.

10-Learning
Directory containing learning notes.

file
Generic term for a document or file.

DATAVIEW
Programming concept or data visualization tool.

table
Generic term for a database table.

evtx-analyst
evtx-analyst is a tool used to parse Windows `.evtx` logs and surface suspicious activity.<SEP>The tool feeds [[windows-event-ids]] to detect suspicious activity.

DFIR
DFIR is the goal of using the evtx-analyst tool.

python-evtx
python-evtx is a Python library that can be used to parse EVTX logs.

windows-event-ids
windows-event-ids is a list of event IDs that the evtx-analyst tool feeds on to detect suspicious activity.<SEP>A wiki page documenting Windows event IDs.

evtx
evtx is the file format of the logs that the evtx-analyst tool parses.

Windows Event IDs
A collection of event codes used for Windows logging and auditing

4624
An account successfully logged on

4625
An account failed to log on

4672
Special privileges assigned to new logon

4688
A new process has been created

4720
A user account was created

7045
A new service was installed

1102
The audit log was cleared

Security
Relates to security-related events

System
Relates to system-related events

Logon Type
Indicates the type of logon (interactive, network, etc.)

Successful logon
Indicates a successful user logon

Failed logon
Indicates a failed user logon

Admin-equivalent logon
Indicates a logon with special administrative privileges

Process execution trail
Indicates the creation of a new process for auditing purposes

Persistence / backdoor account
Indicates the creation of a user account for potential malicious activities

Common persistence and lateral-movement artefact
Indicates the installation of a new service, often used for malicious activities

Anti-forensics red flag
Indicates the clearing of the audit log, often used for malicious activities

MCP server basics
A set of rules and concepts related to MCP server management, including setup, configuration, and troubleshooting.

Windows logon events (4624/4625)
A set of Windows events related to logon activities, including success and failure events.

Goroutines & channels
A set of programming concepts and techniques for using goroutines and channels in Go programming.

Status
A set of possible states or conditions that a learning ledger can have, including `new`, `used`, and `confident`.

Area
A category or field of study that a concept or topic belongs to.

Last checked
A date or timestamp indicating when a concept or topic was last reviewed or updated.

Notes
A field for storing additional comments or explanations related to a concept or topic.

00-Inbox/
A designated area for capturing new notes and ideas, sorted chronologically.

10-Learning/
A repository for detailed learning materials, categorized by topic.

20-Projects/
A collection of project notes, organized by project.

30-CTF-Writeups/
A database of write-ups on Capture The Flag challenges, sorted chronologically.

40-Languages/
A library of notes on various programming languages, organized alphabetically.

50-Reference/
A database of reference materials, organized by category.

90-Meta/
A metadata repository, containing learning ledgers and other relevant information.

flashcards
A technique for memorizing information, utilizing spaced repetition and review.

system
The underlying mechanism for managing notes and ideas.

Rule zero
A guiding principle for capturing notes, emphasizing simplicity and minimal effort.

Daily
A recurring activity for managing notes, taking place every day.

Weekly sweep
A periodic task for reviewing and organizing notes, occurring once a week.
